column3: The Greek keeps John’s disciples and the Pharisees’ disciples in separate clauses, rather than joining them as a single subject.
“Guests of the bridegroom” renders the Greek image “sons of the bridechamber.”
The Greek says “days” and repeats “in those days,” which BSB compresses.
“Sews” makes the method of applying the patch explicit.
The Greek expresses necessity: new wine “must be put” into fresh skins; BSB uses the indicative “is poured.”
BSB’s comparative “better” matches the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “good” (χρηστός).
